newsitem.title: USA: Gateway CFO declines comment on Q2 business.
newsitem.headline: Gateway CFO declines comment on Q2 business.

text.p: Gateway 2000 Inc Chief Financial Officer Dave McKittrick discussed new product plans and strategies aimed at the corporate personal computer market, but declined to comment on how the company's sales were going during the current quarter.
Speaking at a PaineWebber Technology Conference here, McKittrick began his presentation by warning that "there's not going to be comments on business conditions."
"It usually comes in like a lamb and goes out like a lion," he said, repeating the company's common description of how sales typically begin slowly in April, but pick up in June.
He was responding to widespread market rumors that the company had planned to pre-announce a potential earnings disappointment for the quarter ended in June.

During the same presentation, Bill Shea, Gateway's vice president for major accounts, said the company was gearing up to introduce a network PC, targeted at large corporate customer accounts, that would cost around $900 and be introduced in July.

The Pentium-based computers would have a flexible design that would permit corporate network planners to exercise a large measure of control over how software is used in the machines. The computer, known as the E 1000, is designed to meet a growing demand for computers that are easy to manage and lower in cost.

In addition, McKittrick said the company plans to expand beyond its current desktop and laptop computer lines to offer servers, the more powerful category of machine used to manage groups of computers in a network.
"We are going to be in servers," he said, "that's probably a 1998 program."
"But we have made the decision to create a server program," the executive said.
As a leading of direct supplier of PCs, Gateway derives about 49 percent of its revenues from business customers, 38 percent from consumers and the rest from government and education buyers.
